title: Review: The Delivery App
explanation: Level 2 review! This is a food delivery app. Each row is one order: who ordered, from which restaurant, when, the total, the tip, and how many minutes delivery took. Some tips are missing (NULL) because those customers didn't tip. Take a look at the data first, then use everything from Level 2: NULL, math with AS, text and date functions, and CASE WHEN.

lines.explain: Show the customer, plus their total times 2, nicknamed double_total.
Only keep orders from Sushi Spot.

tasks.prompt: Show the customer's name in capital letters (call it loud_name) and the restaurant, for orders with no tip.
tasks.answer: SELECT UPPER(customer) AS loud_name, restaurant FROM deliveries WHERE tip IS NULL;
hints: Two things from Level 2: UPPER() for capitals, and IS NULL for missing tips.
SELECT UPPER(customer) AS loud_name, restaurant ... WHERE tip IS NULL

solution_lines.explain: Show the customer in capitals, nicknamed loud_name, plus the restaurant.
Keep only orders where the tip is missing.

tasks.prompt: For orders that DO have a tip, show the customer and the total plus the tip. Call that column amount_paid.
tasks.answer: SELECT customer, total + tip AS amount_paid FROM deliveries WHERE tip IS NOT NULL;
hints: Add two columns together with +, and filter out the missing tips.
SELECT customer, total + tip AS amount_paid ... WHERE tip IS NOT NULL

solution_lines.line: SELECT customer, total + tip AS amount_paid
solution_lines.explain: Show the customer, plus total and tip added together, nicknamed amount_paid.
Keep only orders with a tip. Adding a number to NULL gives NULL, so we skip those.

tasks.prompt: Show the customer and order date for every order placed in March.
tasks.answer: SELECT customer, order_date FROM deliveries WHERE strftime('%m', order_date) = '03';
hints: Pull the month out with strftime(). March is month 03, and it comes out as text.

solution_lines.explain: Show the customer and order date columns.
Keep orders where the month is 03, meaning March. It's in quotes because strftime gives back text.

tasks.prompt: Show the customer, minutes, and a speed column: 'Fast' if under 20 minutes, 'Normal' if under 40, otherwise 'Slow'. Sort by minutes, quickest first.
tasks.answer: SELECT customer, minutes, CASE WHEN minutes < 20 THEN 'Fast' WHEN minutes < 40 THEN 'Normal' ELSE 'Slow' END AS speed FROM deliveries ORDER BY minutes ASC;
hints: Two WHENs plus an ELSE. Check the fastest first, then sort.
CASE WHEN minutes < 20 THEN 'Fast' WHEN minutes < 40 THEN 'Normal' ELSE 'Slow' END AS speed ... ORDER BY minutes ASC

solution_lines.explain: Show the customer and minutes, plus a new column.
Everything else is Slow. Name the column speed.

tasks.prompt: Predict first: how many rows will this return?
hints: Count two groups: tips under 3, and missing tips. OR means either one counts.
Tips under 3: Hiro and Jay. Missing tips: Ben, Emma, and Isla.

solution_lines.line: WHERE tip < 3 OR tip IS NULL;
solution_lines.explain: Keep orders with a tip under 3 (2 orders) OR no tip at all (3 orders). That's 5. Without IS NULL, the missing tips would be skipped.

recap: Level 2 complete! You can now handle missing values, do math, work with text and dates, and build your own categories.
